WAVE Pilot, Urban Greening Teams Shortlisted for IPAA WA Awards

Discover more

Local news platform
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:48
Instaread

The Department of Water and Environmental Regulation's WAVE Pilot, Program Manager Carolyn Martin and Urban Greening team have been shortlisted for the 2026 IPAA WA Achievement Awards. 

There is a WAVE of excitement across the Department of Water and Environmental Regulation's (the Department) Nature Directorate, with our people and projects shortlisted in multiple categories for the 2026 IPAA WA Achievement Awards.

WA Vegetation Extent (WAVE) Pilot Program Manager Carolyn Martin has been shortlisted for the prestigious Information Technology Practitioner of the Year award, recognising her leadership in bringing together artificial intelligence, environmental science and cross-government collaboration to tackle a longstanding vegetation information challenge.

The WAVE Pilot has also been shortlisted for Best Practice in Digital Transformation and Best Practice in Innovation.

WAVE is testing how satellite imagery, artificial intelligence, machine learning and cloud processing could provide more consistent and repeatable native vegetation mapping across Western Australia. Better vegetation information supports government work ranging from land use planning and environmental approvals to conservation and bushfire preparedness.

There is more recognition for Nature, with the Department's Urban Greening team shortlisted for Best Practice in Collaboration Across Government Agencies for delivering Treebate and the WA Tree Recovery Program.

The programs supported the planting of more than 12,000 trees across Western Australia in 2025-26. Treebate encourages eligible Western Australians to plant native trees on their property, while the WA Tree Recovery Program responded to replacement planting following tree loss caused by polyphagous shot-hole borer.

Working across government, industry and the community, the Urban Greening team helped deliver accessible and coordinated services, including integrating residential rebates into ServiceWA.

Together, the four shortlist places recognise individual leadership, digital innovation and practical cross-government collaboration.

Congratulations to Carolyn, the WAVE Pilot and Urban Greening teams, and the many partners who contributed to their work.
